full_judgment:
8. Mr. Md. Mansurul Hoque Chowdhury vehemently urges that both the courts below were wrong to place reliance upon the evidence of PWs 4 and 5 inasmuch as the search was made and the seizure list was prepared in violation of the provisions of section 103 CrPC. Secondly, the seized 13 bottles of wine not having been sealed there was violation of the mandatory provision of law in this regard and the courts illegally relied upon the report of the Chemical Examiner in convicting the petitioner. Thirdly, the courts below were wrong in not taking into consideration the provisions of sections 77 and 78 of the Excise Act. Fourthly, non-examination of the Chowkidar and the neighbouring shop owners vitiated the trial leading to miscarriage of justice, And lastly, the court of appeal below did not properly appreciate the statements of PWs 4 and 5. 

 11. I shall deal with the last contention of Mr. Chowdhury first. The contention is of no substance as under section 439 CrPC appreciation and re-assessment of evidence of the prosecution witnesses by this court is not called for unless there is a glaring illegality committed by the court of appeal below in arriving at its finding as to the guilt of the accused petitioner leading to miscarriage of justice. I do not find such infirmity in the judgment of the court of appeal below. 

 12. Now let me revert to the first contention. Section 103 CrPC, in my opinion, has no application to the facts of the instant case. This section falls under Chapter VII of the Code. Chapter VII relates to issuance of processes to compel the production of documents and other moveable property and for discovery of persons wrongfully confined. Section 103 relates to search to which process is required to be issued to compel production of the moveable and requires that before making such search the officer conducting the search shall call upon two or more respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched situates to attend and witness the search and the seizure list shall be prepared in their presence and they shall sign the same. In this case the question of compelling the petitioner to produce the country-made wine which is being sold secretly to the officer conducting the search upon secret information does not arise inasmuch as the very issuance of summons to produce the wines in question will frustrate the purpose of the search and no useful result will be had. I think that for the purpose of conducting search in order to find out as to whether a person is guilty of an offence punishable under section 46 of the Excise Act the provision of section 103 CrPC has no application. Moreover, in this case on merit it does not appear from the evidence on record that PWs 4 and 5 were not respectable persons and not of the locality in which the shop situates. PW 4 Moslem Ali is a Director of the Madaripur Central Co-Operative Bank. I can not think that he is not a respectable person. He states that he was present at the time of seizure of 13 bottles from the shop of the petitioner. He was witness to the seizure list. PW 5 Golam Hossain is also a local person. He states that he was present at the time of seizure and saw the seized 13 bottles of wine from the shop of the petitioner and the seizure list was prepared in his presence. Thus it seems that both PWs 4 and 5 proved the seizure list. PW 6 who was acquainted with the handwriting of the Chemical Examiner also proved the report, Ext. 3. So far as his contention on sections 77 and 78 of the Excise Act is concerned I find no substance in view of the facts and circumstance of this case. Equally, the second contention of the learned Advocate has no substance as sealing of the bottles which were already sealed is irrelevant. Ours is not a case of taking sample of goods or article. The report of the Chemical Examiner relates to already sealed bottles and reliance upon the report is no illegality. In view of my finding on the first contention the contention on non-examination of Chowkidar and the neighbouring shop owners also fails.
